request.instruction:
You review a prior-authorization request against a medical policy's criteria.
For each criterion, decide from the evidence alone whether it is:
- "met": the evidence states that the criterion is satisfied,
- "not-met": the evidence states a fact that fails the criterion, such as a value outside a threshold or a date outside a window,
- "insufficient": the evidence does not say, or says it only vaguely, without a date, or as hearsay.
A time stated relative to a dated document, such as days or a week before or after it, is dated.
A statement that is uncertain, conditional or reported second-hand is "insufficient", even when it suggests the criterion fails.
Evidence that does not confirm a criterion is "insufficient", not "not-met".
Cite only references copied exactly from the evidence list (for example "DocumentReference/doc-1").
Never compose a reference from a document's description or a criterion's wording. Do not recommend an outcome.
Respond with JSON only:
{"findings": [{"criterionId": "...", "status": "met" | "not-met" | "insufficient", "evidence": ["..."], "rationale": "..."}]}

criteria.title: Obstructive sleep apnea is diagnosed
criteria.requirement: The member has a diagnosis of obstructive sleep apnea, recorded as a condition or stated by the prescriber.

criteria.title: Continuous pressure was tried and failed
criteria.requirement: The record documents a trial of at least 21 days of continuous positive airway pressure, and the prescriber states that it was not tolerated or did not control the apnea.

criteria.title: Apnea-hypopnea index of 18 or more
criteria.requirement: A sleep study dated within the 12 months before the request reports an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of at least 18 events per hour.

criteria.title: Bi-level settings were shown to work
criteria.requirement: A titration study or the prescriber's note documents that bi-level pressure at the ordered settings controlled the apnea.

evidence.text: Condition: G47.33 Obstructive sleep apnea (adult) (pediatric). Onset 2026-04-15.

Clinical note (Sleep study report, dated 2026-04-15T12:00:00Z):
Split-night polysomnography, 2026-04-15.
Diagnostic portion: apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 42 events per hour.
Impression: severe obstructive sleep apnea.

Clinical note (Prescriber note on the CPAP trial, dated 2026-08-20T12:00:00Z):
CPAP at 14 cm H2O used from 2026-05-01 to 2026-08-15, 107 days.
Download shows residual AHI 21 events per hour and mask leak; she cannot exhale against the
pressure and wakes repeatedly. In my judgement CPAP has not been tolerated.

value.rationale: The member has a recorded condition of obstructive sleep apnea.
The record documents a trial of CPAP for 107 days, and the prescriber states that it was not tolerated and did not control the apnea.
The sleep study dated within 12 months before the request reports an apnea-hypopnea index of 42 events per hour.
There is no evidence documenting that a titration study or prescriber's note shows that bi-level pressure at the ordered settings controlled the apnea.
